newsitem.title: USA: O'Dell death row appeal goes to U.S. Supreme Court.
newsitem.headline: O'Dell death row appeal goes to U.S. Supreme Court.

text.p: Convicted rapist and murderer Joseph O'Dell married a volunteer legal aide on Wednesday as his lawyers filed a last-minute appeal with the U.S. Supreme Court to stop his execution scheduled for later in the day.
Earlier a federal appeals court in Richmond turned down a request for new DNA tests on behalf of O'Dell, saying the claim was "meritless," the Virginia Attorney General's Office said.

O'Dell, whose case has attracted huge interest in Italy and been championed by Pope John Paul II, is due to be executed by lethal injection at 9 p.m. EDT (0100 GMT Thursday) for the 1985 rape and murder of Helen Schartner of Virginia Beach.
In a midday wedding at the Greenville Correction Centre, O'Dell, 55, married Lori Urs, 41, his volunteer paralegal, prison spokesman David Botkins said.

O'Dell remained behind bars and the couple was not allowed to touch. The ceremony was conducted by the Rev. Russell Ford, a former prison chaplain who has known O'Dell for many years. It was O'Dell's fourth marriage, Urs' second.
As his wife, Urs will be entitled to claim his body from the Virginia State Medical Examiners Office.
Botkins said O'Dell had declined a last meal.

"We will still provide him with a tray with whatever the institutional menu is today. He doesn't have any family so his day will consist of legal visits, clergy visits, and then this wedding ceremony," Botkins added.
In their U.S. Supreme Court appeal, O'Dell's lawyers said state-of-the-art testing of semen samples recovered from the victim's body could conclusively prove his innocence.
"There is no legitimate state interest in denying Mr. O'Dell access to this evidence," they said.
Virginia authorities say they intend to go ahead with the execution despite appeals for clemency from Pope John Paul and authorities in Italy, where O'Dell has found wide support.
Police said O'Dell, who was found guilty in 1985, said he abducted, pistol-whipped, raped and strangled the 44-year-old secretary before dumping her body in a field.
The Italian interest has bewildered and annoyed Schartner's family.
"It's just like the Italians hate us," her sister Gail Lee told the Virginia Pilot newspaper."I used to have great respect for that country and its history and its art...now I never want to go there.
"I never want to set foot on their soil. Because by listening to just one side of this case, they in essence have said to my family. 'You are worthless. Helen's life didn't matter."
Just why Italy is so gripped by O'Dell, who has a long criminal record and has no ties to the country, is a mystery.

The Pope and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi have led a chorus of protest against his death sentence. Their appeals have encouraged street protests and vigils, particularly outside the U.S. embassy in Rome.
O'Dell has been made an honorary citizen of the city of Palermo and has said he wants to be buried there if his execution goes forward as planned.
Italy, which has no death penalty in civilian criminal cases, is among the most vocal supporters of a worldwide ban on capital punishment.
Gov. George Allen, a Republican known for his vigorous anti-crime stance, has said he believes O'Dell is guilty and refused to allow new DNA testing in the case.

The condemned man's supporters questioned the testing. A DNA test done on O'Dell's shirt in 1990 showed that blood on it did not belong to O'Dell or Schartner. But tests on the blood on his jacket showed by odds of 166,000 to one that the blood was Schartner's.
O'Dell's "spiritual adviser" is Sister Helen Prejean, author of "Dead Man Walking," the best-selling book that was made into a movie.
